summary.headline: ICRA Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28.4% YoY, led by Research & Analytics (+56.8%) with Fintellix consolidated from October 2025.
summary.overview: ICRA reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 28.4% YoY, with Research and Analytics up 56.8% on the Fintellix acquisition and Ratings up 10.6%. Q4 consolidated PBT before exceptional items and tax was INR 72.8 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 20.4% and PBT grew 10%, with exceptional charges from the new Labour Code excluded for comparability. Management flagged moderation in the Knowledge Services business and a margin-mix shift toward product-led businesses, and it sees near-term bond market softness offset by bank credit growth. Capital allocation questions (buyback, cash of over INR 700 crores, acquisition IRRs) were largely deflected, with the dividend raised and a special dividend declared.

segments.name: Ratings
segments.commentary: Revenue up 10.6% in Q4 and 14.2% for FY26. Management said the segment is a leverage play on economic activity, and Q4 growth was below some peers, which management attributed to a different base and strategic focus on growth segments.

segments.name: Research and Analytics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 56.8% in Q4 and 29.8% for FY26, driven by Fintellix (consolidated from October 2025, roughly 26% EBITDA margin per notes). Excluding Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly; Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily and turned profitable.

segments.name: Knowledge Services (KnowTech)
segments.commentary: Stable in core areas but growth moderated due to discontinued engagements and automation. Management expects a structural margin shift as non-KnowTech businesses, with different margin profiles, gain mix.

segments.name: Moody's-related non-ratings work
segments.commentary: Growth has been muted over the last couple of years and management expects moderation, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Some periodic in-sourcing by the parent continues.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management cited a BankTech product-led EBITDA range of 20% to 35%, depending on geography mix.
Management expects Fintellix to drive reasonable growth over the next 2 to 3 years, partly offsetting Knowledge Services moderation, without quantifying it.
ICRA projects India GDP growth moderating to 6.2% in real terms in FY27, assuming average crude of $95 per barrel.

Management expects bank credit to drive most ratings growth in the near term, with bond market activity subdued due to higher yields; no significant slowdown seen in the first couple of months of FY27.
Bank transition to the expected credit loss framework from 1 April 2027 is expected to sustain demand for risk modelling and compliance solutions.
Management expects roughly INR 180 to 200 crores of cash flow generation in FY27, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.
Research and Analytics reorganised into KnowTech, BankTech and CapTech, supported by a unified IT and product engineering organisation.
Ongoing investment in analytics platforms, compliance capabilities and AI-powered agents; AI layer being integrated into subsidiary analytical tools.
demand_pricing: Ratings demand is tied to bank credit and bond issuance; the first couple of months of FY27 showed no significant slowdown, but geopolitical headwinds persist.
Fintellix competitors cited: Regnology and Nasdaq Technologies (global, PE or public-backed, acquisition-driven), plus system integrators and some Indian CRAs with risk and regulatory solutions.
About USD 18 million of FY26 revenue is dollar-denominated (roughly one-third of about INR 600 crores revenue, per management's figure); dollar-denominated costs are not significant.
Fintellix shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity or subscription model is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Ratings growth materially lower than peers, and what is the non-ratings growth ex-Fintellix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICRA is in a similar band to peers, with double-digit growth over the last 4 years, and that growth-segment focus is the strategy. Ex-Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly while Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration given over INR 700 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a rising dividend (normal dividend INR 60 to INR 70 per share plus special dividend) and said alternative capital allocation options are being evaluated, subject to Board approval and tax changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ratings outlook for FY27, and what are April-May borrowing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bond activity to stay subdued given higher yields, with bank credit driving growth. No significant slowdown was seen in the first couple of months of FY27. No revenue growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&A margins evolve as the mix shifts, and could Ratings margins exceed 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said product-led BankTech-type businesses earn 20% to 35% EBITDA margins, and that double-digit Ratings revenue growth typically brings margin expansion as employee cost growth stays below 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Moody's-related work and in-sourcing from the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been muted and is expected to moderate, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Periodic in-sourcing continues, with new project work arriving on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fintellix segment profit and business description?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give Fintellix-specific contribution, citing parity of disclosure, but referred to notes to accounts showing around 26% EBITDA margin. Fintellix was described as RiskTech and RegTech, covering regulatory reporting and credit analytics for banks, insurers and asset managers.

risks_watch: Elevated energy prices from the West Asia conflict and a possible weak monsoon could weigh on FY27 growth and credit demand.
Knowledge Services growth moderation and automation trends could continue to pressure segment margins during the mix shift.
Limited disclosure of acquisition returns and Fintellix-specific financials, which shareholders have asked about.
Ratings margin gap versus other CRAs; management intends to close it through sales growth.
Capital allocation: whether cash above INR 700 crores is returned to shareholders via buyback or other means, pending Board decision.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Ratings resilience and the Fintellix platform, but cautious on near-term bond markets and the macro outlook. Management was evasive on margin guidance, acquisition IRRs, Fintellix-specific profit and buybacks, deferring to future Board decisions.
key_quotes: We delivered a strong Q4 performance with consolidated revenue increasing by 28.4% year-on-year.
In the first couple of months of this financial year, we have not seen any significant slowdown in the market or generally speaking, in our ratings business.
We don't give a guidance on margin.
We don't give any specific Fintellix contribution.
